people.name: Gabe Evans
people.role: U.S. Representative (CO-08)
people.position: Lead House sponsor of the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340); says states should keep flexibility over rate design.
key_actions: 2026-06-18: Introduced H.R. 9340
Offered the committee substitute narrowing it to data centers
2026-09-16: Bill passed the House 417-3

quote.text: My bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require while giving states the flexibility to determine what works best for their communities.

people.name: Kathy Castor
people.role: U.S. Representative (FL-14)
people.position: Democratic co-lead of H.R. 9340; calls it a first step that lets states set stricter guardrails.
key_actions: Co-introduced H.R. 9340

quote.text: The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act is an important first step that can help lower costs for our neighbors back home and empower states to set additional, strict guardrails.

people.name: Jon Husted
people.role: U.S. Senator (R-OH)
people.position: Senate sponsor of S. 5028 and leader of the push to pass H.R. 9340; in a competitive 2026 race against Sherrod Brown where data centers are an issue.
key_actions: 2026-07-16: Introduced S. 5028
2026-09-17: Sought unanimous consent
Pushed leaders to hold the 2026-09-30 cloture vote

quote.text: In plain language, if you create the cost, you should pay the cost.

people.name: Brian Fitzpatrick
people.role: U.S. Representative (PA-01)
people.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340; also backs the Data Center Transparency Act (H.R. 6984) and a Data Center Bill of Rights resolution (H.Res. 1471).
key_actions: Cosponsored H.R. 9340

quote.text: The Ratepayer Protection Act addresses who pays

people.name: Josh Hawley
people.role: U.S. Senator (R-MO)
people.position: Lead sponsor of the GRID Act; wants data centers on their own power and public reporting of their electricity use.
key_actions: 2026-02-11: Introduced S. 3852

quote.text: American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country.

people.name: Chris Van Hollen
people.role: U.S. Senator (D-MD)
people.position: Lead sponsor of the Power for the People Act; wants FERC-run data center load queues and data center rate classes.
key_actions: 2026-01-15: Introduced S. 3682

quote.text: the huge corporations building and running data centers should cover the costs of the energy they need – not push those costs onto the backs of consumers

people.name: Paul Tonko
people.role: U.S. Representative (NY-20)
people.position: House lead of the Power for the People Act (H.R. 8241); told the Energy and Commerce markup the committee bills did not go far enough.
key_actions: 2026-04-09: Introduced H.R. 8241

quote.text: We are not doing what this moment demands of us,

people.name: Byron Donalds
people.role: U.S. Representative (R-FL); candidate for Florida governor
people.position: Sponsor of H.R. 9777, which would require data centers to run off the grid and off public water.
key_actions: 2026-07-20: Introduced H.R. 9777

quote.text: It’s in their interest to make sure that we can construct these centers, and I think the number one way you address and mitigate the concerns that people are having is to just ensure their utility bills aren’t going up in the process.

people.name: Lisa Blunt Rochester
people.role: U.S. Senator (D-DE)
people.position: Lead Democratic sponsor of the Senate Data Center Transparency Act of 2026.
key_actions: 2026-10-01: Introduced the Data Center Transparency Act of 2026 with Sen. Curtis

quote.text: there is legitimate concern about how these projects could raise utility bills, harm our environment, or impact public health

people.name: John Curtis
people.role: U.S. Senator (R-UT)
people.position: Republican co-lead of the Senate Data Center Transparency Act of 2026.
key_actions: 2026-10-01: Introduced the Data Center Transparency Act of 2026 with Sen. Blunt Rochester

quote.text: Americans are rightly skeptical when a large company tells them not to worry about the impacts of a new data center in their community,

people.name: Angus King
people.role: U.S. Senator and member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee
people.position: Independent who caucuses with Democrats. In July he said talks could not finish until the administration stopped favoring some energy sources over others. On Sept. 30 he said all issues were solved in concept and the work left was drafting language.
key_actions: 2026-07-17: Told POLITICO that negotiators had made progress but the administration had to take its thumb off the scale
2026-09-30: Said that all issues were solved in concept and legislative language was still needed

quote.text: All the issues are solved in concept

people.name: Catherine Cortez Masto
people.role: U.S. Senator and member of the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee
people.position: Led the Senate Democrats' push for permit certainty: a June letter to appropriators asking for riders that bar technology-specific permitting barriers, and the June 16 Senate FREEDOM Act with Sen. Tom Cotton. Her position on the final bill was not found in the sources read.
key_actions: 2026-06-08: Led an ENR Democrats' letter urging fiscal 2027 spending-bill language on fair permitting of solar and wind
2026-06-16: Released the Senate FREEDOM Act with Sen. Tom Cotton (R-Ark.)

quote.text: directs the agencies under your jurisdiction to permit energy projects fairly and without arbitrary technology-specific barriers

sources.title: Senate Dems push spending riders on wind, solar permits

people.name: Brett Guthrie
people.role: Chair, House Energy and Commerce Committee
people.position: Backed the Ratepayer Protection Act as a way to build power for AI responsibly. POLITICO reported on Oct. 1 that he had not endorsed the Senate permitting bill.
key_actions: 2026-06-24: Praised the Ratepayer Protection Act before the Energy and Commerce markup
2026-10-01: Reported by POLITICO as not yet endorsing the Senate deal

quote.text: Winning the race to AI dominance is essential to securing America’s future global leadership, and that means expeditiously building the power infrastructure needed to support new technologies, while doing so in a responsible way.

sources.title: The Mystery of the Ratepayer Protection Act
Senate bipartisan permitting deal faces a House buzz saw

people.name: Teresa Leger Fernández
people.role: U.S. Representative and member of the House Natural Resources Committee
people.position: Skeptical of changing the National Historic Preservation Act. She says the law does not prevent development but requires consultation before building, and that Republicans use long delays to try to wipe out the underlying law. Her view of the final bill was not found.
key_actions: 2026-06-09: Told POLITICO she wanted to preserve the National Historic Preservation Act

quote.text: We want to preserve the National Historic Preservation Act.

sources.title: Debate over preservation law tripping up permitting talks

people.name: Daniel Palken
people.role: Director of Infrastructure for Energy and Permitting, Arnold Ventures
people.position: Former Senate staffer for Whitehouse, Hickenlooper and Manchin. Described the 2026 talks as four-corners negotiations among the EPW and ENR leaders, sorted a deal into six buckets, and named the administration's permit cancellations and withholding as the biggest obstacle to Democratic buy-in.
key_actions: 2026-07-29: Appeared on Heatmap's Shift Key to explain the likely contents of a deal

quote.text: all four parties are really sincerely interested in good faith in getting to a deal

sources.title: What a Permitting Reform Deal Could Look Like (Shift Key)

people.name: Jarrod Agen
people.role: Executive Director, National Energy Dominance Council
people.position: Said in June the administration wants a permitting deal but would not give up good projects for bad ones, and blamed Democrats and New York's Clean Water Act review for blocking gas pipelines.
key_actions: 2026-06-10: Spoke at POLITICO's Energy Summit on permitting reform and the Constitution pipeline

quote.text: We’re not going to give bad projects at the cost of good projects

sources.title: Special edition: POLITICO's Energy Summit kicks off hot permitting summer

people.name: Frank Macchiarola
people.role: Chief Advocacy Officer, American Clean Power Association
people.position: Said in August that ACP wanted negotiators to take time to get it right and was aligned with Democrats who needed a commitment from the administration to permit renewables; he called the Pentagon's stalling of wind approvals a red line.
key_actions: 2026-08-07: Told E&E News that Pentagon stalling of wind approvals is a red line

quote.text: negotiators were smart to push back their timeline for a deal in order to “get it right.”

sources.title: Senators outline future of permitting talks

people.name: Travis Fisher
people.role: Director of Energy and Environmental Policy Studies, Cato Institute
people.position: Libertarian analyst who said conservatives are becoming more comfortable with transmission when it is about load growth and a stronger grid rather than green policy. He also said state regulators have a political interest in acting on large-load tariffs.
key_actions: 2026-07-13: Quoted by E&E News on right-of-center views of transmission
2026-06-23: Quoted by Heatmap on state regulators and the Ratepayer Protection Act

quote.text: In general, the right of center is getting much more comfortable with transmission.

sources.title: The Mystery of the Ratepayer Protection Act

people.name: Ari Peskoe
people.role: Director, Electricity Law Initiative, Harvard Law School
people.position: Critic of the voluntary approach: he called the House Ratepayer Protection Act's PURPA standard largely symbolic because Congress cannot force state regulators to act, and criticized the White House pledge for leaving out utilities and regulators.
key_actions: 2026-06-23: Told Heatmap the Ratepayer Protection Act's PURPA section is largely symbolic

quote.text: largely symbolic

sources.title: The Mystery of the Ratepayer Protection Act

people.name: Alex Epstein
people.role: Author and fossil fuel advocate
people.position: Joined the May dinner with Wright and Republican lawmakers and pushed Congress for a permitting deal covering all forms of energy, including restraining the administration from blocking solar and wind approvals.
key_actions: 2026-05-19: Attended Wright's dinner with Republican lawmakers on permitting

quote.text: I’m against any sort of technology-related crackdown of any kind by any administration

sources.title: Wright meets with Republicans on permitting, but deal remains elusive as ever
